title: Unit – 5 : Session – 9 | Holistic Criteria, Relationship-Based Management and the Transition Plan
sections: Q1. HOLISTIC CRITERIA FOR TECHNOLOGIES AND SYSTEMS: any technology or system must be evaluated on (1) whether it serves a REAL, assessed human need (right utilisation) rather than manufactured want; (2) whether it is PEOPLE-FRIENDLY — safe, dignifying, strengthening competence and relationship; (3) whether it is ECO-FRIENDLY — cyclical, non-depleting, non-polluting; (4) whether it draws on RENEWABLE and local resources, ensuring continuity; and (5) whether it remains within the COMPETENCE and participation of its users, avoiding dependence and centralised control. These criteria apply equally to a machine, a software platform, a production system or a management structure.

Q2. THE FIVE CRITERIA restated as a checklist I can apply: (1) NEED — what real need does it serve, and is that need of the Self or merely of sensation? (2) PEOPLE — who is fulfilled and who, if anyone, is exploited or harmed, including makers and bystanders? (3) NATURE — what does it take from the orders of nature, and does it return in a form nature can use (avartansheel)? (4) CONTINUITY — can it run indefinitely on renewable flows? (5) COMPETENCE — does it develop the user's capability or deepen dependence? A technology passing all five serves the comprehensive human goal; failing any one, it needs redesign, not marketing.

Q3. MANAGEMENT MODEL — FROM CONTROL-BASED TO RELATIONSHIP-BASED: prevailing management treats human beings as 'resources' to be controlled through incentive and surveillance — an extension of the assumption that people are driven only by fear and greed; results: disengagement, attrition, ethical erosion. RELATIONSHIP-BASED management begins from right understanding: every member is a co-existence of Self and Body with the same natural acceptance; the manager's role is GUIDANCE (ensuring right understanding and competence) and CARE (ensuring facility), evaluation is on intention-plus-competence, and the organisation's goal is mutual fulfilment of all stakeholders — workers, customers, society, nature. Trust replaces surveillance as the operating system; productivity follows fulfilment rather than pressure.

Q4. MY TRANSITION PLAN TO VALUE-BASED LIFE AND PROFESSION: (1) SELF — daily self-exploration (10 min): audit one desire/decision for its source (sensation/preconditioning/natural acceptance); weekly written self-evaluation against the value-policy-character trio. (2) FAMILY — practise evaluation of intention over competence; take responsibility for one act of guidance or care weekly; discuss the family goal in terms of mutual happiness and prosperity, not income alone. (3) STUDY→PROFESSION — choose projects and, later, an employer/venture whose work passes the five holistic criteria; apply the mutual-fulfilment check to everything I build. (4) SOCIETY/NATURE — one socially relevant project per year (study → model → implementation), and daily right-utilisation habits (waste segregation, water and energy restraint, cycling). REVIEW: each semester, honestly assess progress and correct course — the transition is a direction, not an event.
